problems.title: Counting with the map
hints: Prefixes: 0, 1, 3, 4, 6, 7; count earlier prefixes equal to current − 3.

problems.title: Divisible by k
problems.statement: Count subarrays with sum divisible by 5 in [4, 5, 0, −2, −3, 1].
hints: Prefix sums mod 5; pairs of equal residues.

problems.title: Why not a window
problems.statement: Subarray sum equals k with negative numbers.

parts.prompt: Why does a sliding window fail?
options: Extending a window can decrease the sum, so you can't tell when to shrink

problems.solution: Without monotonicity, the shrink decision isn't safe; prefix sums plus a map don't need it.

problems.title: Difference array
problems.statement: Array of 6 zeros; add 2 to [1, 3], add 5 to [2, 5], add −1 to [0, 2].
hints: d[l] += v, d[r + 1] −= v, then prefix-sum.
problems.solution: Index 2 is in all three ranges: 2 + 5 − 1 = 6. Index 5 only in the second: 5.

problems.title: 2-D prefix sums
problems.statement: Grid [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9]]. S[r][c] = sum of the rectangle from (0, 0) to (r − 1, c − 1).

parts.prompt: Sum of rows 1–2, columns 1–2 via S?

problems.title: Longest subarray with sum k
problems.statement: To find the longest (not count) subarray summing to k with a prefix map…
hints: Longest means the start is as early as possible.
problems.solution: Earliest index: length = j − first[P[j] − k]. Don't overwrite it.

problems.title: Equal 0s and 1s
problems.statement: Longest subarray of a binary array with equally many 0s and 1s.

options: Map 0 → −1, then longest subarray with sum 0

problems.solution: As ±1: −1, 1, −1, −1, 1, 1, −1; prefixes 0, −1, 0, −1, −2, −1, 0, −1. Prefix 0 at 0 and 6 → length 6; prefix −1 at 1 and 7 → 6. Answer 6.
